title: 《巫师3》开发团队用 AI 帮助波兰配音演员在中风后重演杰洛特
content:
Polish voice actor for Geralt returns for The Witcher 3 with AI
Production
Audio
News
Witcher 3 devs use AI to help Polish voice actor reprise role of Geralt after stroke
After a stroke left him unable to do the voice of the Witcher series' main character anymore, Jacek Rozenek consented to using AI for Witcher 3's next expansion.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 13, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via CD Projekt Red
Original Polish voice actor for
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
protagonist Geralt of Rivia Jacek Rozenek has consented to a special exception for CD Projekt Red to use AI to aid his voice acting in the announced expansion to the 11-year-old game, specifically for the purpose of maintaining continuity in his performance after his voice was changed following a stroke.
As reported by
Game File
, the discussion began when CDPR brought Rozenek in to discuss returning for the upcoming expansion,
Songs of the Past
. As an unprecedented late expansion to the 2015 game, the new lines would be in close proximity to thousands of lines Rozenek had recorded as the Polish voice of Geralt well over a decade ago, but due tohis stroke, Rozenek sounds different. Thus, the decision was made to use AI to bridge the gap.
Rozenek had returned to acting in the years after his stroke, but the job drained him physically, and he sounded gruffer and lower than he had years prior. In a brand new project, maybe that wouldn't make a big difference, but it would have been immediately noticeable when positioned next to recordings from a decade prior.
Related:
GenAI-using developers say they mostly employ it for 'research and brainstorming'
CD Projekt Red made the decision to call on Respeecher,
a professional AI voice generator that the studio has used before
to use the voice of a late actor in
Cyberpunk 2077's
Phantom Liberty
expansion. Rozenek agreed, allowing the studio to take his recordings for
Songs of the Past
—which he was still being hired and paid for—and use AI to make it sound more like it used to. The AI tools involved were trained on Rozenek's previous recordings over the prior Witcher games.
"I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good," says localization producer Mikołaj Szwed. Szwed stresses this is not a common occurrence and this exception was only being made due to Rozenek's health.
It is unknown if Rozenek will reprise the role of Geralt in the Polish version of
The Witcher 4
, but a different, deeper voice for Geralt might make more sense in a sequel rather than an expansion to an older game.
